strings.name: Candace Parker
strings.role: Retired basketball player, sports executive and analyst
strings.summary: Candace Parker expanded ideas of position through ball-handling, passing, shooting and rim protection. She won WNBA MVP and Rookie of the Year together, titles with three different teams and two Olympic golds. After retiring in 2024, she continued broadcasting and sports business, entering the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A WNBA champion and MVP whose versatile skills broadened women’s basketball’s influence.

strings.facts.f1.value: St. Louis, Missouri, United States; raised in Naperville, Illinois

strings.facts.f2.value: University of Tennessee, sport management graduate, 2008
strings.highlights.h1.title: Three teams’ titles and two MVPs
strings.highlights.h1.text: Championships in Los Angeles, Chicago and Las Vegas; regular-season MVP in 2008 and 2013.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Versatility and continuing involvement
strings.highlights.h2.text: Two Olympic golds; after retirement, broadcasting and adidas Women’s Basketball leadership.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Naismith Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.t1.text: Formally inducted August 15 and delivered her speech.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Retirement and new role
strings.timeline.t2.text: Announced retirement in April and became adidas Women’s Basketball president in May.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Third franchise championship
strings.timeline.t3.text: A member of the champion Aces, but a foot injury kept her out of the later season and playoffs.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Chicago Sky title
strings.timeline.t4.text: Returned to her home region and helped win the franchise’s first championship.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Sparks championship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Helped Los Angeles win and received Finals MVP.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Second regular-season MVP
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won the league award again with the Sparks.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First pick and rookie MVP
strings.timeline.t7.text: Joined the Sparks first overall and won MVP, Rookie of the Year and Olympic gold.
strings.timeline.t8.title: College national title
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won with Pat Summitt’s Tennessee team, then again in 2008.
